specs.goal: Every Item stored by the toy API carries a third field, created_at: a server-generated ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed, millisecond precision, e.g. "2026-09-10T17:00:00.000Z") recorded at the moment the item is created. The Item shape becomes exactly { id, name, created_at }, and that full shape is returned by POST /items (201), GET /items, and GET /items/:id (200). The timestamp is assigned once, by the server, from the system clock at creation time; it is never re-derived on read, never mutated, and never taken from client input. All other behavior is unchanged: id assignment and its non-consumption on rejected requests, name validation (400 "name is required" for missing/empty/non-string, 400 "name too long" above 64 UTF-16 code units), 404 "not found" semantics including non-canonical integer ids, JSON content types, and the GET /health body. The existing suite in toy/test/items.test.js compares Items API-response-to-API-response (e.g. assert.deepEqual(list, [item])), so those assertions remain valid rather than breaking; they must be extended — not weakened or deleted — so the new field is actually asserted instead of silently carried along, and any assertion enumerating an Item's keys must now expect created_at.
risk_reasons: rule: surface kind schema: Item = { id: number, name: string, created_at: string (ISO-8601 UTC, Z-suffixed, millisecond precision) }
Additive field only — adds created_at without removing or changing id or name
No external consumers — toy venture with internal-only use
Backward-compatible — existing clients expecting id and name still receive them
Not irreversible — timestamps are generated fresh per instance at creation time
No auth, secrets, payments, or infra touched
Guidance explicitly states additive field additions are low blast radius

specs.goal: Add an optional `tags` field to the toy Item. `POST /items` accepts an optional `tags` key whose value must be an array of 1–32 character strings with at most 10 entries; any other value is rejected with 400 `{ "error": "invalid tags" }` and no state change. Accepted items store `tags` (defaulting to `[]` when the key is absent) and every representation of an Item — the `POST /items` 201 body, `GET /items` entries, and the `GET /items/:id` body — carries exactly the keys `id`, `name`, `tags`. Existing name validation, ids, insertion order, `GET /items/:id` 404 behavior and `GET /health` are unchanged.
risk_reasons: rule: surface kind schema: Item = { id: number, name: string, tags: string[] }
Additive field addition: specs explicitly classify additive fields as low-risk
No external clients: toy venture with no external consumers means no existing client contracts to break
Backwards compatible: new tags field in responses is safe for clients that don't use it to ignore
No infrastructure changes: purely in-memory data model expansion, no auth/secrets/payments/infra touched
Existing contracts preserved: name validation, id sequencing, insertion order, health endpoint, and 404 behavior all unchanged
Reversible: data model change can be rolled back without irreversible consequences
